newsitem.title: USA: United's salaried, management win wage adjustment.
newsitem.headline: United's salaried, management win wage adjustment.

text.p: United Airlines, the chief oeprating subsidiary of UAL Corp, said Friday a mid-contract wage agreement was approved for its salaried and management employees.

Management will receive two base salary increases of four percent in both July of 1997 and 1998, the carrier said. They will also participate in a three-year profit-sharing plan that could pay an additional amount in 1998, 1999 and 2000, the company said.

Meanwhile, salaried employees will receive five-percent salary increases in July of this year and in July of 1998, United said. Certain salaried employees will also receive a one-time payment in August representing 5.42 percent of the employee's actual earnings between January 1, 1997 and June 30, the company said.
Yesterday, United's union machinists approved a wage agreement that provides two five-percent wage increases in July of 1997 and 1998.
United's union pilots have yet to vote on a similar tentative wage agreement reached earlier this month.
UAL shares closed up 1/2 Friday at 67-1/8.
